options.name: allow_compression
options.description: The compression mode allowed by this OpenVPN server. Compression can potentially increase throughput but may allow an attacker to extract secrets if they can control compressed plaintext traversing the VPN (e.g. HTTP)

options.name: api_host
options.description: The hostname or IP address of the pfSense device.

options.name: api_key
options.description: An API key to use for authentication.

options.name: api_password
options.description: The password to authenticate with the pfSense API.

options.name: api_port
options.description: The port number of the pfSense API.

options.name: api_protocol
options.description: The protocol to use when connecting to the pfSense API.

options.name: api_username
options.description: The username to authenticate with the pfSense API.

options.name: authmode
options.description: The name of the authentication server to use as the authentication backend for this OpenVPN server

options.name: caref
options.description: The `refid` of the CA object to assume as the peer CA.

options.name: cert_depth
options.description: The depth of the certificate chain to check when a certificate based client signs in. Certificates below this depth are not accepted. This is useful for denying certificates made with intermediate CAs generated from the same CA as the server. Set to null to use system default.

options.name: certref
options.description: The `refid` of the certificate object to assume as the OpenVPN server certificate.

options.name: client2client
options.description: Enables or disables allowing communication between clients connected to this server.

options.name: connlimit
options.description: The number of concurrent connections a single user can have.

options.name: create_gw
options.description: The gateway type(s) that will be created when a virtual interface is assigned to this OpenVPN server

options.name: custom_options
options.description: Additional options to add to the OpenVPN server configuration.

options.name: data_ciphers
options.description: The encryption algorithms/ciphers allowed by this OpenVPN server.

options.name: data_ciphers_fallback
options.description: The fallback encryption algorithm/cipher used for data channel packets when communicating with clients that do not support data encryption algorithm negotiation (e.g. Shared Key).

options.name: description
options.description: The description for this OpenVPN server.

options.name: dev_mode
options.description: The carrier mode for this OpenVPN server. `tun` mode carries IPv4 and IPv6 (layer 3) and is the most common and compatible mode across all platforms. `tap` mode is capable of carrying 802.3 (layer 2).

options.name: dh_length
options.description: The Diffie-Hellman (DH) parameter set used for key exchange.

options.name: digest
options.description: The algorithm used to authenticate data channel packets, and control channel packets if a TLS Key is present.

options.name: disable
options.description: Disables this OpenVPN server.

options.name: dns_domain
options.description: The default domain to provide to clients.

options.name: dns_server1
options.description: The primary DNS server to provide to clients.

options.name: dns_server2
options.description: The secondary DNS server to provide to clients.

options.name: dns_server3
options.description: The tertiary DNS server to provide to clients.

options.name: dns_server4
options.description: The quaternary DNS server to provide to clients.

options.name: duplicate_cn
options.description: Enables or disable allowing the same user to connect multiple times.

options.name: dynamic_ip
options.description: Enables or disables allowing connected clients to retain their connections if their IP address changes.

options.name: ecdh_curve
options.description: The Elliptic Curve to use for key exchange. The curve from the server certificate is used by default when the server uses an ECDSA certificate. Otherwise, secp384r1 is used as a fallback.

options.name: gwredir
options.description: Enable forcing all client-generated IPv4 traffic through the tunnel.

options.name: gwredir6
options.description: Enable forcing all client-generated IPv6 traffic through the tunnel.

options.name: inactive_seconds
options.description: The amount of time (in seconds) until a client connection is closed for inactivity.

options.name: interface
options.description: The interface or Virtual IP address where OpenVPN will receive client connections.

options.name: keepalive_interval
options.description: The keepalive interval parameter.

options.name: keepalive_timeout
options.description: The keepalive timeout parameter.

options.name: local_network
options.description: The IPv4 networks that will be accessible from the remote endpoint. Expressed as a list of one or more CIDR ranges or host/network type aliases. This may be left blank if not adding a route to the local network through this tunnel on the remote machine. This is generally set to the LAN network.

options.name: local_networkv6
options.description: The IPv6 networks that will be accessible from the remote endpoint. Expressed as a list of one or more CIDR ranges or host/network type aliases. This may be left blank if not adding a route to the local network through this tunnel on the remote machine. This is generally set to the LAN network.

options.name: local_port
options.description: The port used by OpenVPN to receive client connections. Valid options are: a TCP/UDP port number

options.name: lookup_fields
options.description: The list of fields to use when looking up existing resources. This should be a list of field names that uniquely identify a resource.

options.name: maxclients
options.description: The maximum number of clients allowed to concurrently connect to this server.

options.name: mode
options.description: The OpenVPN server mode.

options.name: netbios_enable
options.description: Enables or disables NetBIOS over TCP/IP.

options.name: netbios_ntype
options.description: The NetBIOS node type.

options.name: netbios_scope
options.description: The NetBIOS Scope ID. This provides an extended naming service for NetBIOS over TCP/IP. The NetBIOS scope ID isolates NetBIOS traffic on a single network to only those nodes with the same NetBIOS scope ID.

options.name: ntp_server1
options.description: The primary NTP server to provide to clients.

options.name: ntp_server2
options.description: The secondary NTP server to provide to clients.

options.name: passtos
options.description: Enables or disables setting the TOS IP header value of tunnel packets to match the encapsulated packet value.

options.name: ping_action
options.description: The action to take after a ping to the remote peer times-out.

options.name: ping_action_push
options.description: Enables or disables pushing the ping action to the VPN client.

options.name: ping_action_seconds
options.description: The number of seconds that must elapse before the ping is considered a timeout and the configured `ping_action` is performed.

options.name: ping_method
options.description: The method used to define ping configuration.

options.name: ping_push
options.description: Enables or disables push ping to the VPN client.

options.name: ping_seconds
options.description: The number of seconds to accept no packets before sending a ping to the remote peer over the TCP/UDP control channel.

options.name: protocol
options.description: The protocol used by this OpenVPN server.

options.name: push_blockoutsidedns
options.description: Enables or disables blocking Windows 10 clients' access to DNS servers except across OpenVPN while connected, forcing clients to use only VPN DNS servers.

options.name: push_register_dns
options.description: Enables or disables running `net stop dnscache`, `net start dnscache`, `ipconfig /flushdns` and `ipconfig /registerdns` on connection initiation for Windows clients.

options.name: remote_cert_tls
options.description: Enables or disables requiring hosts to have a client certificate to connect.

options.name: remote_network
options.description: IPv4 networks that will be routed through the tunnel, so that a site-to-site VPN can be established without manually changing the routing tables. Expressed as a list of one or more CIDR ranges or host/network type aliases. If this is a site-to-site VPN, enter the remote LAN/s here. May be left empty for non site-to-site VPN.

options.name: remote_networkv6
options.description: IPv6 networks that will be routed through the tunnel, so that a site-to-site VPN can be established without manually changing the routing tables. Expressed as a list of one or more CIDR ranges or host/network type aliases. If this is a site-to-site VPN, enter the remote LAN/s here. May be left empty for non site-to-site VPN.

options.name: serverbridge_dhcp
options.description: Enables or disables clients on the bridge to obtain DHCP.

options.name: serverbridge_dhcp_end
options.description: The bridge DHCP range's end address.

options.name: serverbridge_dhcp_start
options.description: The bridge DHCP range's start address.

options.name: serverbridge_interface
options.description: The interface to which this TAP instance will be bridged. This is not done automatically. This interface must be assigned and the bridge created separately. This setting controls which existing IP address and subnet mask are used by OpenVPN for the bridge.

options.name: serverbridge_routegateway
options.description: Enables or disables pushing the bridge interface's IPv4 address to connecting clients as a route gateway.

options.name: sndrcvbuf
options.description: The send and receive buffer size for OpenVPN. Set to null to use the system default.

options.name: state
options.description: Whether the resource should be present or absent.

options.name: strictusercn
options.description: Enables or disables enforcing a match between the common name of the client certificate and the username given at login.

options.name: tls
options.description: The TLS key this OpenVPN server will use to sign control channel packets with an HMAC signature for authentication when establishing the tunnel.

options.name: tls_type
options.description: The TLS key usage type. In `auth` mode, the TLS key is used only as HMAC authentication for the control channel, protecting the peers from unauthorized connections. The `crypt` mode encrypts the control channel communication in addition to providing authentication, providing more privacy and traffic control channel obfuscation.

options.name: tlsauth_keydir
options.description: The TLS key direction. This must be set to complementary values on the client and server. For example, if the server is set to 0, the client must be set to 1. Both may be set to omit the direction, in which case the TLS Key will be used bidirectionally.

options.name: topology
options.description: The method used to supply a virtual adapter IP address to clients when using TUN mode on IPv4.

options.name: tunnel_network
options.description: The IPv4 virtual network used for private communications between this server and client hosts.

options.name: tunnel_networkv6
options.description: The IPv6 virtual network used for private communications between this server and client hosts.

options.name: use_tls
options.description: Enables or disables the use of a TLS key for this OpenVPN server.

options.name: username_as_common_name
options.description: Enables or disable the username of the client being used in place of the certificate common name for purposes such as determining Client Specific Overrides.

options.name: validate_certs
options.description: Whether to validate SSL certificates when connecting to the API.

options.name: verbosity_level
options.description: The OpenVPN logging verbosity level.

options.name: wins_server1
options.description: The primary WINS server to provide to clients.

options.name: wins_server2
options.description: The secondary WINS server to provide to clients.
